research.title: Measuring AI Agents as Teammates with Collaborative Intelligence
research.why: Most significant question for a general reader in the window: as AI agents move into shared work, a 240-task benchmark finds even top models have collaboration weaknesses that are separate from how capable they are alone. Fresh angle (not covered in the last 8 weeks; 10-10 'tool-using agents fail' and 10-31 'Memory Tax' are about solo agent failures, not teamwork). arXiv primary. Preprint, label 'not yet peer-reviewed'. Scores came from the abstract only, so the dossier must read the full paper for numbers.

news.title: Anthropic shares progress on provable inference: cryptographically proving which model produced an output
news.why: Most significant news item whose primary source was actually fetched (HTTP 200). It addresses a basic trust question for anyone using AI through an API or app: was the answer really produced by the model you were promised? Not political, no geography, and not covered in the last 8 weeks. The 10-24 Anthropic piece was about formal verification of software, which is a different subject. Attribute as Anthropic's claims. Original reporting: https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/03/anthropic-is-working-on-a-system-to-prove-ai-models-identity/

invention.title: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: frontier LLMs can read and write neural network weights
invention.why: This is the only strong invention candidate whose primary source was fetched and confirmed (the authors' own MIT CSAIL blog). It is a striking demo: language models editing another network's weights directly instead of training it. It leans toward research, but it is a hands-on demo blog post, not a paper, so it fits the invention slot, and it does not collide with the arXiv research pick. Honest caveat: a blog post with no peer review or independent replication; report what the authors say they showed. Not covered in the last 8 weeks (Qwenputer, 10-31, is a different project).
